title: I Love Zugzwang❤️
reviewNotes: Four branches from the full six-piece diagram. Source king-first Re4 Ka2 Re2+ Kb1 Rg2 route and mating response are preserved. Pawn-first path uses explicitly independent Re2+ Kb1 connecting checks, then Rxg2 reaches the separately illustrated five-piece zugzwang; three responses mate. No jump between source resets is presented as a move.
transcript: How can the white rook stop the two black pawns that are about to promote? You see, this is the 31st of May Sunday puzzle from chess.com and it is quite the head scratcher because if we try for example to give a check to the black king, now after the king moves, we can't even stop the pawn. If we stay here, we're going to lose the rook and if we go back, the pawn is now in time to promote because the black rook is going to help it. If we give a check on B4, we have the same exact problem. So, it might seem like the best thing that white can do is go behind [music] the pawn and make sure to stop it. But, this at best is a draw. Black is going to move. We do [music] win the pawn, but now the rook is free and with the only pawn left on the board, black is the only one playing for a win here. So, is that it? Is this position a draw? Well, not exactly. White has a surprising way to win starting with rook to E4. This move prepares to meet G2 with rook to E1 check forcing the king up and then winning the [music] pawn with a fork. But, not only that, this is actually checkmate in one by force. Black is in zugzwang. The only setup that avoids the checkmate is the exact position that black is in. For example, if the king moves here, this is a checkmate. If the pawn pushes, this is a checkmate and if the rook goes up, this is a checkmate. Every single move sets black up for failure. So, black cannot allow that and instead he should try to move the king away right away. And now it might seem like black is out of the woods. You cannot come down here because the rook is defending and if you go behind the pawn, the rook is going to come to defend the pawn. But, of course, we can still give this check. And the only move for the black king is to come back down. And believe it or not, we can achieve the same setup after the very precise rook to G2. This position is incredible because black's downfall came about because of his extra material. If it wasn't for these two pawns, there would be no way to checkmate Black. This is yet again the same zugzwang. This pawn cannot be pushed, and we already saw that any other move played with these three pieces will inevitably lead to a checkmate.
